scene.metaphor: A small handmade research vessel representing LightTag is docking beside a larger, smoother partner vessel representing Primer, showing acquisition as a clean merger without losing the smaller boat’s distinct shape.
scene.setting: A polished studio tabletop seascape built from cool-gray acrylic water, matte slate surface, and a softly blurred horizon of layered gray backdrop; the whole scene feels like a miniature harbor staged for an editorial portrait.
scene.frozen_incident: Tal, recognizable by his dark curly hair and salt-and-pepper beard, leans in from the left with a calm, satisfied half-smile as he guides the small vessel into a perfect side-by-side dock; the moment freezes just as a tiny magnetic fender clicks the two hulls together with a harmless splash.
physical_materials: one restrained warm coral accent on Tal's shirt
semantic_anchors: larger partner vessel nearby and clearly more substantial
Tal as a recognizable human operator
cool-gray foundation with cobalt and mint accents
avoid: text or letters on hulls or dock
scene.image_instruction: Create a polished editorial studio photograph of a miniature harbor on a cool-gray tabletop. Tal Perry appears as a recognizable operator on the left: dark curly hair, salt-and-pepper beard, warm eyes, relaxed half-smile, wearing a single restrained coral tank top accent. He gently guides a small handmade LightTag vessel made of chipboard and balsa toward a larger, sleeker Primer vessel, both in a lateral 3:1 composition. The LightTag boat must keep its distinct silhouette while docking cleanly alongside the larger craft; freeze the instant a tiny magnetic bumper clicks and a faint ripple spreads across acetate water. Use cobalt and mint accents on ropes, trim, and dock posts, with the rest in cool grays and slate tones. Lighting should be crisp studio key light with soft shadow separation, high tonal contrast, and generous negative space. Keep only three large supporting props: the dock, the larger vessel, and a subtle crane or bollard. The scene must remain readable as one dominant subject at thumbnail size and feel calm, celebratory, and precise.
